sourceChecks.claim: Azure separates an initial accepted response from asynchronous completion and a status/result endpoint, supporting the delayed-result contract and explicit failure observation.

RabbitMQ states publisher confirms and consumer acknowledgements cover independent boundaries; acknowledgements permit retiring a delivery and loss can lead to redelivery. Neither verifies arbitrary application effects.
AWS requires a stable caller operation identifier with durable atomic mutation/recognition; this supports database-effect deduplication without a universal delivery guarantee.

Azure distinguishes transient failures from nonrecovering errors and recommends delayed, bounded retries. Isolation/replay policy is a design choice also supported by the competing-consumer poison-message guidance.

Azure warns about ordering and poison messages and describes keyed sessions/single-consumer processing. Serializing dependent effects is the stated design rule; idempotency alone is not claimed to restore order.

Azure explicitly requires downstream rate controls, warns against unbounded consumer scaling, and notes sustained excess arrival growth and finite storage/retention. The subtraction example follows directly.
Kafka design documents independent consumer positions, rewind, partition assignment and external-effect coordination. Retention bounds replay and partition ordering is not global ordering.
